criteria.justification: The response clearly directs the team to disable the inclusion logic if a verified isolating flag is confirmed within 30 minutes, otherwise to execute a full rollback. The hard time box and explicit default prevent indecision during the active incident.

It characterizes disablement or rollback as a “cheap and reversible mitigation” that returns production to a known-good state and allows a properly tested relaunch, contrasting this with a rushed hotfix’s unknown, potentially compounding harm. It also checks for non-revertable schema or configuration changes before rollback and provides a fallback between the two mitigation mechanisms.

The response explicitly contrasts confirmed harm accruing every hour across existing customers with the bounded communications and early-adopter cost of pausing a feature launched only hours earlier. It concludes that leaving core risk signals wrong for days would cause greater customer and reputational damage than retracting the announcement.

It rejects an emergency hotfix because engineering has said a proper fix takes days and a minimally tested calibration patch could turn the incident into “a second high-sev.” The recommendation instead uses a verified flag or rollback while the proper fix is developed and tested.

The response provides a detailed sequence after mitigation: verify live traffic, update the incident channel and status page, brief support, notify affected customers, remediate already-fired signals, conduct a post-incident review, and relaunch with regression tests and staged monitoring.
